name: Spice Bag

cookwares.name: spice mill or mortar and pestle
large wok or carbon steel skillet

ingredients.name: chicken bouillon powder, such as Knorr or Lee Kum Kee
japanese-style karaage, prepared according to package directions
british-style chips, prepared according to package directions
neutral oil, such as canola or peanut
red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded, and thinly sliced
chili crisp, such as Lao Gan Ma, plus more as needed

instructions.primary_message: For the Spice Blend: In a small mixing bowl, whisk ground Sichuan peppercorns, garlic powder, onion powder, five-spice, white pepper, sugar, MSG, chicken bouillon powder, and Sichuan chili flakes to combine. Season to taste with additional garlic powder, sugar, and/or chili flakes as desired; set aside.

For the Curry Sauce: In a small saucepan set over medium heat, melt butter. Whisk in flour and curry powder and cook, stirring frequently, until lightly browned and fragrant, 3 to 4 minutes. Add warm chicken broth, whisking to combine, and cook, stirring frequently, until glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes. Season to taste with salt. Reduce heat to lowest setting and cover to keep warm, stirring occasionally.
For the Chicken and Potatoes: Season karaage or chicken nuggets and chips or fries with 2 teaspoons of reserved spice blend, tossing to evenly coat; set aside.

For the Stir-Fry: In a large wok or carbon steel skillet set over medium-high heat, heat oil until shimmering. Add onion and pepper, and cook, stir-frying until edges are lightly charred and vegetables have softened, about 5 minutes. Add chicken and potatoes to the wok, and season with 2 teaspoons spice blend and chili crisp. Using a spatula, toss ingredients in wok to evenly coat with chili oil and spices, about 1 minute.
Transfer mixture to a wide, shallow bowl, and serve alongside curry sauce for dipping.

description: In this beloved Dublin takeout dinner, crunchy chicken, fluffy chips, and a numbing, spicy coating—plus curry sauce for dipping.
notes:
Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → store-bought low-sodium chicken broth; japanese-style karaage → 340 g frozen breaded chicken breast nuggets; british-style chips → 340 g frozen bagged steak fries

Notes: Sichuan chili flakes may also be labeled as Chinese chili flakes at your Asian grocer.
If you plan to make the Japanese-style karaage for this recipe, the final product may be slightly less crispy than if you choose frozen nuggets. I actually appreciate the slightly crunchier, more durable coating that frozen chicken nuggets, such as the ones sold at Costco, bring to the table.
The same goes for the British-style chips — if you make your own, they’re a little more likely to fall apart than frozen steak fries, while frozen fries will have a slightly drier exterior. Both are great in this recipe.

Make-ahead and storage: Both the curry sauce and spice blend recipes make more than you’ll need for one spice bag. The extra spice blend will keep for weeks—and actually get better as the chili oils infuse into the rest of the mix—and the curry sauce can be stored in the freezer for about a month. When you need to use it, add to a saucepan with 1/4 cup water and simmer on low until it comes back to life, whisking occasionally.
author: Amy McCarthy
